![](./media/logo.webp){fig-alt="repo-operator logo" width="40%" fig-align="center"}

[`repo-operator`](https://github.com/ioaiaaii/repo-operator) is a Make library that provides a single, versioned set of
targets for operating a collection of repositories: container images, Go, Helm charts, changelogs, and repository
hygiene. Targets execute their tooling in containers pinned by content digest, and consumer repositories incorporate the
library as a Git submodule.


## Background

The name and design draw on two concepts from mathematics and physics.

**Hermitian operators.** In quantum mechanics, observables are represented by Hermitian operators, whose eigenvalues are
real, so every measurement yields a well-defined value. The name plays on *hermetic* builds, a principle of
[release engineering](https://sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering/) in which a target is a pure function of its
declared inputs and produces the same output regardless of who runs it, where, or when.

**Non-locality.** A non-local operator determines its value at a point from a function over its *entire domain*, rather
than from that point's neighbourhood. Likewise, a target's behaviour in a repository is determined not by that
repository's Makefile or host, but by a single shared definition.


## Motivation

Software projects accumulate a common layer of build and operational logic. When each repository maintains this layer
independently, the implementations diverge, and their behaviour becomes coupled to the tool versions installed on
individual machines. A correction to a security scan must then be repeated in every repository, and repositories that
are updated less often continue to run outdated toolchains without any visible failure.

`repo-operator` treats this layer as a versioned dependency. A change is made once, in the library, and each consumer
adopts it by advancing its submodule reference on its own schedule.


## Design

- **Hermeticity.** Tools run in containers pinned by `sha256` digest, so local and CI executions use identical tool
  versions. The exceptions are `op-go-build` and `op-go-mod-*` (host Go), `op-precommit-install` (host
  `pre-commit`), and `op-image-build` (host `buildx`). The outputs are tool-deterministic rather than bit-for-bit
  reproducible, since the containers reach the network and artefacts carry the commit and build time.
- **Targets as functions.** Targets take parameters at invocation, such as `make op-image-build IMAGE_NAME=my-app`, so
  one target serves every image and every repository.
- **Naming.** Targets are named `op-<domain>[-<action>]` after their module, and private variables carry the `OP_`
  prefix. Public parameters are unprefixed and declared with `?=`, so a value from the consumer Makefile, the command
  line, or the environment takes precedence over the default.
- **Self-documentation.** `make op-help` renders every target and public parameter, with its declared default, from
  `##v` and `##p` annotations kept next to the definitions.


## Usage

The host requires `docker` with `buildx`, `make`, and `git`. Add the library as a submodule, conventionally under
`build/`:

``` bash
git submodule add https://github.com/ioaiaaii/repo-operator.git build/repo-operator
```

Then set parameters, include the library, and define targets in terms of its interface. `all.mk` includes every
module; a subset starts with `core.mk`.

``` makefile
OPERATOR_PATH  := build/repo-operator
VERSION_PKG    := github.com/myorg/my-service/pkg/version

include $(OPERATOR_PATH)/makefiles/all.mk

help: op-help

##@ App

.PHONY: app-image
app-image: ## Build the application image.
	@$(MAKE) --no-print-directory op-image-build IMAGE_NAME=my-app
```

A complete example is in
[`examples/basic`](https://github.com/ioaiaaii/repo-operator/blob/master/examples/basic/Makefile).

### Extending

Public parameters are overridden in the consumer Makefile before the `include`, or at invocation, because several are
expanded when the library is parsed. `LD_FLAGS` is the exception and can be overridden only at invocation or after the
`include`.

``` bash
make op-image-build IMAGE_NAME=my-app IMAGE_TAG=dev
```

Consumer targets annotated with `##`, grouped under `##@` sections, appear in `make op-help` alongside the library
targets. A recipe can enforce its own parameters with `$(call require,NAME)`, which stops with the name of the missing
parameter:

``` makefile
##@ Database

.PHONY: db-migrate
db-migrate: ## Run database migrations.
	$(call require,DB_URL)
	./scripts/migrate.sh
```

### Versioning

Consumers pin the submodule to a release, and an upgrade is committed in the parent repository:

``` bash
git -C build/repo-operator checkout v1.2.0
git add build/repo-operator && git commit -m "chore: pin repo-operator to v1.2.0"
```


## Reference

The tables list required parameters and those that change behaviour; `make op-help` lists all of them. `<repo>` denotes
the name of the directory in which `make` runs.

### Core

| Target | Description |
|---|---|
| `op-help` | List every target and public parameter |
| `op-env` | Print the resolved tag, branch, version, and commit |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `OPERATOR_PATH` | Path from the repository root to the submodule. Default: `.` |
| `SRC` | Go source root. Default: `.` |
| `BUILD_PATH` | Build tree containing `ci/` and `package/`. Default: `build` |
| `DEPLOY_PATH` | Chart tree. Default: `deploy` |
| `DEFAULT_BRANCH` | Release branch, for tag detection and commit linting. Default: `master` |
| `VERSION` | Version for image tags and binary stamps. Default: the branch name, or on a detached HEAD the `vX.Y.Z` tag at the tip of `DEFAULT_BRANCH` |

### Go

| Target | Description |
|---|---|
| `op-go-lint` | Run `golangci-lint` with `$(BUILD_PATH)/ci/.golangci.yml` (v2 schema) |
| `op-go-test` | Run `go test ./...` |
| `op-go-build` | Build a static binary, using the host Go toolchain |
| `op-go-mod-update` | Update dependencies, then run `go vet` |
| `op-go-mod-sync` | Run `go mod tidy`, `vendor`, and `verify` |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `CMD_PATH` | Main package sources, relative to `SRC`. Default: `cmd/<repo>/*.go` |
| `BINARY_PATH` | Output binary. Default: `$(BUILD_PATH)/<repo>` |
| `GOOS`, `GOARCH` | Target platform. Default: `linux`, `amd64` |
| `VERSION_PKG` | Package declaring `BuildVersion`, `BuildHash`, and `BuildTime`, stamped at link time. A wrong path yields an unstamped binary without an error |

### Image

| Target | Description |
|---|---|
| `op-image-lint` | Lint the Dockerfile with `hadolint` |
| `op-image-build` | Build the image, or build and push it with `IMAGE_MODE=publish` |
| `op-image-digest` | Print the digest recorded by the last build |
| `op-image-run` | Run the image as the container `IMAGE_NAME`, publishing its exposed ports |
| `op-image-inspect` | Analyse layer efficiency with `dive` |

| Mode | Platforms | Output | Attestations |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local` (default) | Host architecture | Loaded into the daemon | None |
| `publish` | `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64` | Pushed to the registry | Provenance and SBOM |

: {tbl-colwidths="[20,28,28,24]"}

`publish` requires a `docker-container` builder with QEMU (`docker buildx create --use`).

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `IMAGE_NAME` | **Required.** Image name. The Dockerfile defaults to `$(BUILD_PATH)/package/<IMAGE_NAME>/Dockerfile` |
| `IMAGE_REPO` | Registry and namespace, e.g. `ghcr.io/myorg`, or a Docker Hub account name. Required for `publish` |
| `IMAGE_TAG` | Default: `VERSION` with characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9.]` replaced by `-` |
| `IMAGE_EXTRA_TAGS` | Additional `--tag` flags, e.g. `--tag ghcr.io/myorg/app:latest` |
| `IMAGE_BUILD_ARGS` | `--build-arg` flags. The default passes `LD_FLAGS`, which an override must repeat |

### Scan

`op-scan` runs Trivy with the subcommand in `TRIVY_ARGS`. The cache must lie inside the mounted `SRC`, and images are
scanned from a `docker save` archive:

``` bash
make op-scan TRIVY_ARGS="fs --cache-dir build/ci/.cache/trivy --exit-code 1 --severity HIGH,CRITICAL ."
```

### Chart

| Target | Description |
|---|---|
| `op-chart-lint` | Run `ct lint --all` with `$(BUILD_PATH)/ci/.chart-testing.yaml`, whose `chart-dirs` lie under `DEPLOY_PATH` |
| `op-chart-test` | Run `ct lint-and-install --all` against the current `~/.kube/config` context |
| `op-chart-package` | Package a chart into `dist/` |
| `op-chart-push` | Push a packaged chart to an OCI registry |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `CHART_DIR` | **Required** by `op-chart-package`. Chart directory, relative to `DEPLOY_PATH` |
| `CHART_PACKAGE` | **Required** by `op-chart-push`. Package file name in `dist/` |
| `CHART_OCI_REPO` | **Required** by `op-chart-push`. Target, e.g. `oci://ghcr.io/myorg/charts` |
| `KUBECONFIG` | Mounted by `op-chart-package` and `op-chart-push`, relative to the repository root. Pass `KUBECONFIG=` if the shell exports an absolute path |

### Changelog

| Target | Description |
|---|---|
| `op-changelog-lint` | Lint commits from `origin/<DEFAULT_BRANCH>` to `HEAD` with commitlint |
| `op-changelog` | Lint, then generate `CHANGELOG.md` with git-chglog |
| `op-changelog-release` | Generate release notes for the required `TAG` |

Configurations are read from `build/changelog/`. The library's own directory, including its two templates, serves as a
starting point once `repository_url` is changed.

### OpenAPI and OpenTelemetry

| Target | Description |
|---|---|
| `op-openapi-docs` | Render the required `OPENAPI_FILE` as Markdown into the required `OPENAPI_DOCS_PATH` |
| `op-otel-up` | Run a local OpenTelemetry Collector in the foreground with `build/ci/.otel-collector-config.yaml`, publishing OTLP on `4317` and `4318` |

### Repository Hygiene

| Target | Description |
|---|---|
| `op-gitignore-sync` | Append the Go, macOS, and Terragrunt templates to `.gitignore` |
| `op-precommit-sync` | Append the `base`, `helm`, and `terragrunt` hook configurations to `.pre-commit-config.yaml` |
| `op-precommit-install` | Sync, then run `pre-commit install` on the host |

Both syncs append template lines without parsing the destination file, so they are run once, when a repository adopts
the library.
